messages:
customer_acme_ops: Hey team — we just wired up an Interface VPC Endpoint to reach api.redwood-inference.com from our prod VPC. From inside the VPC calls are failing with TLS cert errors (curl: certificate subject name does not match target host). The public endpoint is fine. This started right after we created the endpoint + enabled Private DNS. Any quick checks?

maria_support: Thanks — can you paste the output of `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com` from an instance inside the VPC and `curl -vk https://api.redwood-inference.com/health` (redact tokens)? Also which region and VPC endpoint id?

customer_acme_ops: Region: us-west-2, vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h. dig gives `10.0.12.45`. curl output (snip):
* Connected to 10.0.12.45 (10.0.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject name (CN) `internal-nlb-1234.local` does not match target host name `api.redwood-inference.com`
* Closing connection 0

eng_jordan: This is a classic split-horizon / cert SNI mismatch. Quick theory: your Private hosted zone or the interface endpoint DNS is resolving the public hostname to the endpoint ENI/NLB IP, but the backend that's terminating TLS is presenting a cert for an internal name (e.g., internal NLB/ALB CN). The TLS check fails because the cert CN/SAN doesn't include api.redwood-inference.com. Can you run this from the instance to confirm SNI behavior?

1) `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.45:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts`
2) `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.45:443 -servername internal-nlb-1234.local -showcerts`

If the first command still returns the internal cert, the TLS was terminated before SNI was honored or the service behind the endpoint is using the wrong cert.

customer_acme_ops: Ran openssl: first command shows cert CN=internal-nlb-1234.local. second is the same. So looks like TLS is terminated and internal cert used. We didn't change certs. We did create a Private Hosted Zone for api.redwood-inference.com when enabling Private DNS on the endpoint (AWS auto-created a zone).

infra_sam: Two things to check:
- Did you create any Route53 private hosted zones previously for api.redwood-inference.com in this account? If so there can be conflicting records.
- Is the endpoint pointing at a regional NLB that performs TLS termination? PrivateLink connections typically preserve SNI to the service but if the service is fronted by an ALB that terminates TLS and uses internal certs you can get this mismatch.

Also run: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values=*vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h* --region us-west-2` and paste the ENI IDs so we can capture traffic.

maria_support: Another quick workaround while we debug: you can use curl --resolve to force the public hostname to private IP and verify behaviour while keeping SNI in the request: `curl -vk --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:10.0.12.45 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health` — note that --resolve sets Host header + SNI; but if the backend still presents internal cert it's a server-side issue.

customer_acme_ops: ENIs: eni-0abc111def22ghi33. We attempted the --resolve and got same cert mismatch. So server isn't returning the public cert.

eng_jordan: Ok thanks. Two likely remediations:
1) If you can control the backend (your ALB/NLB behind the PrivateLink), update the TLS certificate to include the public hostname (api.redwood-inference.com) as a SAN, or terminate TLS on the NLB with the correct cert.
2) If not, ask us to re-provision the endpoint pointing at the correct Redwood service name — sometimes customers accidentally created a Private Hosted Zone that maps the public name to a different internal ALB (leftover from beta infra). Deleting the conflicting private hosted zone and re-creating the endpoint with "Enable Private DNS" will make the interface endpoint resolve to Redwood's PrivateLink NLB which presents the proper cert.

maria_support: To help us verify: can you share the Route53 private hosted zones list `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` and `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZXYZ` for the zone that contains api.redwood-inference.com? Redact any sensitive records. Also, capture a short tcpdump on the ENI (we only need TLS handshake bytes): `sudo tcpdump -i eni-0abc111def22ghi33 -c 200 -w /tmp/vpce-handshake.pcap port 443` then upload.

customer_acme_ops: We found an older private hosted zone `api.redwood-inference.com` from a prior migration. It pointed to an internal ALB we no longer own. We deleted the private hosted zone and recreated the endpoint DNS. After that `dig +short` now returns `10.0.45.67` (different IP) and `curl -vk https://api.redwood-inference.com/health` returns HTTP 200 and valid cert (CN/SAN includes api.redwood-inference.com). :tada:

maria_support: Awesome — glad that fixed it. Two followups to avoid future surprises:
- Avoid creating private hosted zones that shadow vendor public names unless you intend to route to your own internal endpoints.
- If you must shadow, ensure the backend certs include the public hostnames or use SNI-aware passthrough.
- If you need a list of Redwood PrivateLink service names / expected private DNS behavior we can send the doc link (it lists the service name per region and the IP ranges for our control plane egress if you need egress allowlists).

customer_acme_ops: Please send the doc link. Also, is there anything we should add to our egress allowlist for auth/billing calls? We have a very strict egress policy.

eng_jordan: We'll DM you the recommended minimal outbound destinations (hostnames/IPs and ports). Typically only HTTPS (443) to our control plane endpoints is needed. If you have strict NAT/proxy settings, ensure the NAT allows TLS SNI and that proxies don't replace certs.

deploybot: Incident INC-9876 created for tracking docs update and adding a KB entry about private hosted zones shadowing Redwood PrivateLink services.

maria_support: Closing the thread in >48h if no further issues. Thanks for the quick troubleshooting and for sharing the hosted zone output — that made the root cause obvious. :white_check_mark:
